title: Install Orbit sync journal — week of 2027-04-12
content:
Purpose: lightweight weekly log for the Install Orbit project — ephemeral notes from syncs, live blockers, and the hotlist for field engineers. Aim is to reduce meeting churn by surfacing short decisions and owners.

Context recap (one line): Install Orbit is the on-prem/VPC install profile targeted at mid-market healthcare and fintech customers that require KMS/HSM integration, strict egress controls, and a 2-region failover pattern. This week we focused on two customer installs (Arbor Health PDX and Helios FinServ FRA), a telemetry gap in KV cache metrics, and an emergent MTU mismatch class of failures.

This week's highlights:
- Arbor Health (PDX) completed rack-power and BMC validation; network handed to customer infra team Friday AM. Dataplane tests failed intermittently with packet fragmentation on long prompt loads (observed after ~12k token sessions).
- Helios FinServ (FRA) hit KMS attestation timeout when retrieving key metadata from their HSM cluster; fallback to software KMS allowed install to continue but we blocked before data-plane validation.
- Telemetry: agent-side KV cache hit-rate not reported for ~36 hours due to a schema change in our metrics forwarder (wasn't picked up by the edge pipeline).
- Networking pattern: MTU mismatch surfaced on two installs — symptom is slow token-generation tail latency spikes at iteration >1000 that correlate with TCP retransmits.

Standup snippets (short form):
- Aisha: sync'd with Arbor on firewall ACLs; requested packet capture and promised we will triage with infra on Monday. Created PD-4279.
- Marco: narrowed MTU cases to jumbo frames disabled on customer switches; temporary workaround is forcing GSO off on CUDA hosts — perf regressed ~8-10% in throughput but stabilizes latency.
- Dana: raised PR to add KV-cache metric shim; PR linked above. Need one more review from observability.
- Ethan: Helios escalated HSM vendor to their PKI team; vendor indicated an unsupported endpoint for our client; engineering to provide alternative attestation path.
- Sofia: ran canary against internal replica using 2.4.1-quant build with prefix cache warmup; observed cache warmup lag at cold start — added sequence length telemetry to isolate.

Hotlist (priority order):
1) MTU mismatch mitigation (owner: Marco Liu) — immediate customer impact at Arbor and another prospective. Work: document host-level GSO/TCP offloads shim, add install-time network check to installer (PD-4112), and coordinate with Solutions Eng to get switch config. ETA: hotfix doc and check-in by 2027-04-14. Status: in_progress.
2) HSM/KMS attestation fallback (owner: Ethan Park) — ensure safe fallback to software KMS is explicit in install playbook and gated behind opt-in. Work: write fallback playbook, add telemetry flag for fallback events, update Legal on acceptable fallback per Helios contract. ETA: 2027-04-20. Status: blocked-by-customer-pki.
3) KV cache telemetry schema fix (owner: Dana Brooks) — landed PR but missing observability review. Work: review, deploy to staging, validate metrics stream for three installs. ETA: 2027-04-15. Status: review_pending.
4) Packet-capture and analysis for Arbor (owner: Aisha Patel) — need full capture across edge router and first-hop switch. Work: coordinate with Arbor netops for scheduled window (they prefer Sundays). ETA: scheduled 2027-04-18. Status: waiting_on-customer.

Detailed notes / investigative logs:
- Arbor PDX details:
  - Initial symptoms: token tail lat spikes after ~12k token sessions on 2xA40 nodes with 48GB RAM, producing more than 4k token responses per minute.
  - Observed retransmit spikes using netstat and tcpdump on host facing NIC. Customer switch config: 1500 MTU, they use a mix of older Juniper EX series.
  - Network hypothesis: large UDP-like bursts from our runtime's inter-host communication are being fragmented; although our transport is TCP, large frames from kernel offload interplay cause retransmits.
  - Temporary mitigation: Marco applied 'ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off' on the CUDA hosts; tail latency stabilized over a 30-minute run but throughput dropped ~9%. Need to make decision: tolerate perf hit for first 48 hours of install or force switch config change.
  - Action items: get switch config from Arbor (Aisha), add an installer preflight network MTU check (Marco), log MTU mismatch event in installer with remediation suggestions (Dana).

- Helios FRA details:
  - Failure: KMS attestation returned 504 from customer HSM proxy during key listing. HSM vendor logs show ephemeral auth-token misalignment between their PKI and our attestation client.
  - Workaround performed: manual key export to local vault and use software KMS for initial validation. This is acceptable short-term but requires contract sign-off for longer use.
  - Next steps: Ethan to draft fallback runbook and propose an attestation retry/backoff strategy. Also need to schedule joint debugging call with Helios PKI team (blocked until vendor confirms engineering contact).

Telemetry & observability (notes):
- Root cause for missing KV-cache metric: a protobuf field rename on the agent broke the forwarder mapping. Dana's shim reintroduces the legacy field while we transition. We should add a CI test that validates the metrics pipeline contract.
- Missing token-level tracing in installer logs — observed on two internal canaries where sequence-level tracing was disabled to reduce noise. Decision: enable sequence tracing for first 24h post-install in staging and add a sampling knob for production.

Risks and tradeoffs discussed:
- Making host-level offload changes (GSO/GRO/TCO) stabilizes latency but decreases throughput. For latency-sensitive customers we should prefer switch config changes; for short installs we can accept host changes. Tradeoff logged in PD-4279.
- Allowing software KMS fallback expedites installs but creates a long-term compliance and key custody risk. Need legal/infosec sign-off before we make it the default.

Decisions made this week:
- Installer will surface MTU mismatch with an explicit remediation block and suggested switch config on next minor release (2.4.2). Owner: Marco.
- Enable temporary software KMS fallback as an opt-in flag during install. Owner: Ethan to document and product to add opt-in UI in Console.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Can we implement a kernel-level TCP heuristic in the runtime to avoid retransmit storms without turning off GSO? (open for SRE/serving-runtime deep-dive).
- Can Legal sign off on fallback for regulated healthcare customers in a limited-window 72-hour install exception? (Aisha to own escalation).

Action items (short checklist):
- Marco: submit installer preflight MTU check PR and add remediation text (ETA 04-14).
- Dana: finish observability review and deploy shim to staging; add CI test for metrics contract (ETA 04-15).
- Ethan: draft KMS fallback playbook + markup for Console opt-in and escalate to Legal (ETA 04-20).
- Aisha: schedule packet-capture window with Arbor netops and get switch config export (ETA 04-18).
- Sofia: run two more cold-start canaries with prefix-warmup telemetry enabled; capture trace for >2k sequence runs (ETA 04-16).

Meeting cadence / attachments:
- Next Install Orbit sync: Tue 2027-04-20 10:00 PDT (optional invite for Solutions Eng if MTU mitigation changes).
- Attachments: raw tcpdump from Arbor (uploaded to secure bucket, link in PD-4279), latest installer log bundle for Helios (attachment ref PD-4210).

Notes to self: try small experiment on runtime side to break large send into ~1436 byte chunks at user-space level and benchmark — might avoid kernel offload toggles if effective.

End log.
